rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for becoming visibly red in the face.

example.english: I blush as soon as I see them.
example.jyutping: ngo5 jat1 gin3 dou2 keoi5 zau6 min6 hung4

rows.note: Use this for the visible reddish flush on someone's face, especially from embarrassment or shyness; it is the all-purpose noun for that sense.

example.english: A blush rose on their face, and they looked really embarrassed.
example.traditional: 佢面上泛起一片紅暈，睇落好尷尬。
example.jyutping: keoi5 min6 soeng6 faan6 hei2 jat1 pin3 hung4 wan4 tai2 lok6 hou2 gaam1 gaai3

rows.note: Use this for the cosmetic applied to the cheeks, rather than for the natural redness of a blush.

example.english: This blush looks very natural when applied to the face.
example.traditional: 呢盒胭脂搽上面好自然。
example.jyutping: ni1 hap6 jin1 zi1 caa4 soeng5 min6 hou2 zi6 jin4

rows.note: Use this for the pale pink colour itself, including the pink part of a colour flush and the fashion or makeup colour.

example.english: I want to paint the room blush.
example.traditional: 我想將房間油做淡粉紅色。
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 zoeng1 fong2 gaan1 jau4 zou6 daam6 fan2 hung4 sik1

rows.note: Use this for a subtle colour tone or cast in a painting, design, or other visual work, especially when the colour may be blue, pink, or grey.

example.english: This painting has a cool grey blush to its colour palette.
example.traditional: 呢幅畫帶住一種冷冷哋嘅灰色色調。
example.jyutping: ni1 fuk1 waa2 daai3 zyu6 jat1 zung2 laang5 laang5 dei6 ge3 fui1 sik1 sik1 diu6
